task: Compare blood glucose level distributions across three patient groups (Diabetes / Stroke / CKD) after age filtering (30-70) and removal of zero/missing glucose, using Kruskal-Wallis H test with Dunn post-hoc (Bonferroni) and a density histogram figure.
objective: Determine whether unified blood glucose (mg/dL) differs across the three disease cohorts and, if so, which pairs differ; deliver output.csv (test results table) and output.png (overlaid density histogram with KW p-value).

Healthcare-Diabetes.csv.format: CSV with header, 2768 data rows, 10 columns
Healthcare-Diabetes.csv.notes: Pima-style data; 0 in Glucose encodes missing -> must be dropped, not averaged in.

healthcare-dataset-stroke-data.csv.format: CSV with header, 5110 data rows, 12 columns

key_columns.glucose: avg_glucose_level (mg/dL, float, no missing in this file)

healthcare-dataset-stroke-data.csv.notes: bmi has 'N/A' strings but is irrelevant; only age + avg_glucose_level are needed.

Chronic_Kidney_Disease/chronic_kidney_di.format: ARFF; 24 comment/attribute header lines then '@data' at line 145 (1-based); 400 data instances, 25 attributes
Chronic_Kidney_Disease/chronic_kidney_di.notes: '?' is the missing token (applies to bgr and age). Profile flagged 3 malformed data lines with 26 fields; parsing must be positional-safe (skip or repair rows whose field count != 25) so numeric fields cannot shift.

data_profile.json.role: Upstream schema/profile artifact; used to confirm column names, dtypes, missing token conventions and expected row counts. Not to be modified.

column_unification.unit_check: All three sources are already mg/dL (Diabetes 44-197, Stroke 55-272 typical, CKD 70-490 per profile): no unit rescaling; only dtype coercion to float.
column_unification.output_long_table: Concatenate three DataFrames with columns [source, glucose, age]; reset index.

order_of_operations: 1. Load each dataset, coerce glucose/age to numeric with errors='coerce' ('?' and '' -> NaN).
4. Drop rows with missing glucose or glucose == 0 (also guard negatives -> treat as invalid).
5. Concatenate, attach source label, recheck final per-group n.
filtering_rules.tolerance: Final n per group must be within a small tolerance of the profile counts; larger deviation means a parsing/filter bug -> investigate before testing.

qa_checks: No NaN/0 left in glucose after filtering; min glucose > 0.
Per-group n and median/q1/q3 reported (Diabetes ~125, Stroke ~92, CKD ~123 mg/dL) as a sanity cross-check against the profile.
CKD row count equals 400 instances parsed; malformed 26-field lines logged and excluded (or last-field repaired) so 'bgr'/'age' never shift.
Confirm no duplicates introduced by concatenation and that source labels are exactly the three expected strings.

statistical_plan.test_choice_rationale: Glucose is continuous but strongly right-skewed with unequal variances/group sizes (CKD max 490, Stroke min 55) -> non-parametric one-way Kruskal-Wallis H test instead of ANOVA; robustness to non-normality and heterogeneous scale.

post_hoc.method: Dunn's test: rank all N=4464 observations, compute mean rank per group, tie-corrected rank variance, z = (mean_rank_i - mean_rank_j) / sqrt(var * (1/n_i + 1/n_j)), two-sided normal p-value.
post_hoc.adjustment: Bonferroni over the 3 pairwise comparisons (p_adj = 3 * p_raw, capped at 1.0)
post_hoc.note: CKD is the group with the highest mean rank in the profile (mean 151 vs 108 vs 130), so its z-scores come out negative relative to the other two; sign is kept as computed.

statistical_plan.software: scipy (kruskal), numpy/scipy.stats.norm for Dunn; no scikit-posthocs dependency required -> implement Dunn manually for reproducibility and to control adjustment/capping.

expected_results_reference.use_of_reference: Cross-check only; final numbers must be recomputed from data, not copied from the profile.

output.csv.formatting: no index; statistic and p_value as full-precision floats (scientific notation preserved); significant written as Python bool literals 'True'/'False'.

output.png.type: overlaid density histogram (histogram with density normalization, not a KDE curve)
output.png.annotation: Kruskal-Wallis H and p-value text placed on the axes (upper-right), e.g. 'Kruskal-Wallis H = 628.13, p = 4.01e-137' with scientific formatting to avoid a long decimal string.

labels.title: Blood glucose distribution by patient group (age 30-70)

output.png.extras: legend with group n, edgecolor on bars for readability, tight_layout, dpi=150

acceptance_criteria: output.csv has exactly 5 lines (header + 4 rows), exact column names/order and exact test/comparison strings.
significant column contains only True/False literals.
output.png exists, is a valid PNG, contains three overlaid histograms in red/blue/green and the KW p-value text.
All reported numbers traceable to a rerun of the analysis script on the workspace data.
risks_and_fallbacks: ARFF malformed rows (26 fields): parse manually (split on ','), skip rows with wrong field count and log the count; do not let pandas misalign columns.
CKD '?' tokens: must be mapped to NaN before numeric coercion, otherwise floats fail or become strings.
Extremely small p-values (1e-137) may be printed as 0.0 if formatted with %.4f -> always use full float/repr or scientific notation.
If the overall KW test were non-significant, skip Dunn and output only the KW row (not expected here).
Group imbalance (2885 Stroke vs 273 CKD): note in reporting that rank-based tests weight groups by n; conclusions stay about distributional location.
execution_steps: Step 1: load_and_unify.py - parse 3 files, unify [source, age, glucose], apply filters, save glucose_long.csv + cleaning counts.
Step 2: stats.py - KW test, conditional Dunn + Bonferroni, write output.csv.
Step 3: plot.py - overlaid density histogram, annotate KW p, write output.png.
Step 4: verify_artifacts.py - re-read output.csv/output.png, assert schema/strings/bool dtype and PNG integrity.
